According to SOP-02 (Weekend Shutdown), a reflow oven in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating — 25.2 kW — continuously for as long as it stays on, whereas a properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend. That idle draw is the largest single source of weekend idle energy, so ovens must be switched fully OFF (after the 30-minute post-line warm-down, and only when no boards are inside) rather than left in standby.

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend: about 1,556 kWh versus about 346 kWh normal, an excess of about 1,210 kWh from a single oven. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

Note: the documents state the excess energy (~1,210 kWh) but do not give a dollar cost for it, so I can't provide the NT$ figure from the documents.

answer:
Per SOP-03 Step 2 (the shed playbook order):

- **Shed first:** EV charging — pause EV-01 (100% of its load) [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]
- **Never shed:** the server room, running molders mid-cycle, or reflow ovens with boards inside [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

The full shed order is: (1) pause EV charging EV-01, (2) delay next burn-in loading BI-01/BI-02, (3) raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C CH-01/CH-02, (4) lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar AC-01/AC-02/AC-03.
